Findings:
- The European Commission started enforcing AI Act transparency rules on 2 August 2026, requiring AI systems like chatbots to inform users and deepfakes to be labeled with machine-readable marks. [https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-starts-enforcing-ai-act-rules-and-new-transparency-requirements-2-august]
- The US White House introduced a voluntary AI oversight framework (executive order finalized June 2, 2026) allowing government access to covered frontier models for up to 30 days before release; major AI firms met in early August for safety testing discussions. [https://www.aiandnews.com/blog/ai-regulations-august-2026/]
- The US "Great American AI Act" stalled in the House Judiciary Committee on August 7 over state preemption clause, leaving state AI laws like Colorado SB-205 and California Frontier AI Safety Act active. [https://cubbbix.com/blog/ai-regulation-august-2026-global-update/]
- China's Cyberspace Administration issued 12 fines totaling 4.2 million RMB in first weeks of enforcing companion AI rules effective July 15, 2026. [https://cubbbix.com/blog/ai-regulation-august-2026-global-update/]
- The UK AI Regulation and Safety Bill cleared the House of Commons, with Royal Assent expected by October 2026. [https://cubbbix.com/blog/ai-regulation-august-2026-global-update/]
- India finalized a statutory AI liability framework for its fall parliamentary session after closing feedback on Digital India Act. [https://cubbbix.com/blog/ai-regulation-august-2026-global-update/]
- UK supermarket Sainsbury's paused its AI facial recognition system after a wrongful shoplifting accusation, highlighting retail AI challenges. [https://www.aiandnews.com/blog/ai-regulations-august-2026/]
